text: Applicants must have a minimum overall average of 60 percent with 50% in English 30-1 and 50% in Mathematics 30-1.
Applicants may meet academic requirements through a free academic assessment or placement test.
Applicants must have a minimum overall average of 65 percent in the following high school courses: English 30-1 and Mathematics 30-2 and Three subjects from Group A, B, C or D.
Competitive average for recent years has been in the low 80s. Admission average is calculated using five required Grade 12 subjects.
Admission requires English 30-1 or 30-2 and Mathematics 30-2 (or equivalent).
Applicants must complete English 30-1 and Mathematics 30-2 prior to admission.

Minimum entrance requirements: **High School Course Pathway:** - Grade 12 Language Arts (English 30-2) - Grade 12 Mathematics (Math 30-2 or Applied Math 30) - Three additional Grade 12 courses (at the 30-1, 30-2, 30, or 35 level (5-credit only)) - An overall minimum average of 65% in the five required high school courses. - Proof of English Language Proficiency.

Minimum entrance requirements: A two-year diploma in an IT program related to the selected major, an overall minimum GPA of 2.3, and coursework completed within five years of the application date. Applicants who do not have a two-year diploma may be eligible if 60 post-secondary credits have been completed. Proof of English Language Proficiency is required.

Minimum entrance requirements: Successful completion of a diploma or degree in an accredited engineering technology, information technology, applied science or health science program with a minimum GPA of 2.7. Proof of English Language Proficiency is required. Admission considerations include acceptable programs such as Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, Mechanical Engineering Technology, and Software Development.

Trades to Degrees gives certified trades professionals a direct route into the third year of the Bachelor of Business Administration program. Applicants build on their trade background to move into management and leadership roles.
Applicants may be waitlisted because the program is competitive and seats are limited.
Applicants may present electives from various groups depending on stream and pathway.

Applicants must have English Language Arts 30-1 at 60 percent or English Language Arts 30-2 at 70 percent, Mathematics 20-1 at 60 percent or Mathematics 20-2 at 70 percent or Mathematics 30-1 at 50 percent or Mathematics 30-2 at 60 percent, and Biology 30 at 60 percent. Applicants may also meet academic requirements through a free academic assessment. English language proficiency requirements such as IELTS, TOEFL, Duolingo, CAEL, and Pearson may also apply.

Applicants must have a minimum overall average of 65 percent in the following high school courses: English 30-1 or English 30-2, Mathematics 30-1 or Mathematics 30-2, and Three subjects from Group A, B, C or D. Notes: A maximum of two Group B subjects may be presented and a maximum of one Group D subject may be presented.

Admission average uses five required Grade 12 subjects: English Language Arts 30-1 and four subjects from Group A, Group B, or Group C, with a maximum of one Group B subject. Mathematics 30-2 may be used. Applicants to Nursing must also complete the CASPer test.
Applicants must present English Language Arts 30-1 and four subjects from Group A, Group B or Group C. A maximum of one Group B subject may be presented.
Applicants must present English Language Arts 30-1, Mathematics 30-1, two of Biology 30, Chemistry 30, Mathematics 31 or Physics 30, and one subject from Group C.
